images.caption: Figure 1:Environment Overview.(a)The fly policy is trained in an environment with obstacles and multiple odor sources.(b)The policy is then evaluated in a tethered-ball environment where the fly is head-fixed. The angular and forward velocities are read from the ball, analogous to the biological experiment ofBrezovec et al. (2023).(c)The policy receives olfaction as a weighted sum of intensities sampled at the antennae and maxillary palps.(d)The policy’s proprioceptive input comes directly from NeuroMechFly and includes joint angles, joint velocities, and body-frame gravity, height, and linear and angular velocities.(e)Vision is also provided to the policy by simulating the ommatidia mapping of pale and yellow type cells to pixels.

Figure 2:Agent Architecture Overview.(a)The FlyGym simulator provides visual, proprioceptive, and olfactory observations from a biomechanically realistic fly body. Modality-specific CNN and MLP encoders embed these observations into a shared representationϕt\phi_{t}, which is provided to the actor–critic and intrinsic drive module. When applicable, the policy is additionally conditioned on a sampled skillzz. The intrinsic drive module computes an intrinsic reward from the encoded state transition and selected action. The actor outputs a categorical distribution over discrete motor primitives, while the critic estimates the state value. The policy selects a new motor primitive every 100 ms.(b)Locomotor primitives are translated into joint-level commands by a low-level central pattern generator (CPG) controller, while grooming is executed using a kinematic replay. These motor commands are applied within the FlyGym physics simulation, which is integrated with a timestep of 100μ\mus. Thus, each policy action is executed for 1,000 physics steps before the next action is selected.

Figure 4:Turning Bias.(a)Distribution of turning bias across evaluation rollouts for each method. Points indicate individual rollouts, with the mean and range shown for each method. DIAYN produces a broad distribution of turning biases spanning more of the fly-to-fly variability than the other evaluated methods. Methods with a rollout containing no turns or turns in only one direction are excluded becauselog⁡(NR/NL)\log(N_{R}/N_{L})is undefined for those rollouts.(b)Virtual x-y trajectories integrated from the ball state of the nine flies and the nine DIAYN evaluation skills drawn from a common origin.

(2023), the IPS of the fly brain has an interhemispheric relationship of z-scored activity that is correlated with angular (interhemispheric difference) and forward velocity (interhemispheric sum).(b)As a functional analogue of the bilateral supercluster pairs inBrezovec et al. (2023), we use PCA to find principal components in the network activation of the LSTM layer of the Actor in the policy whose difference correlates with angular velocity and whose sum correlates with forward velocity. This structural relationship appears in DIAYN’s Actor LSTM layer(b)but, does not appear in(c)the randomly initialized DIAYN model.(d)We rank each IDM by the mean of the squared Pearson correlations of its angular and forward heatmaps with the fly’s. Higher is a closer match.
